sources.name: CWE-Bench-Java
sources.license: MIT (dataset repository; upstream projects have their own licenses)
frameworks: Java OSS projects including Spark Java, WildFly, Eclipse Vert.x, Spring Cloud, Apache Camel, Apache NiFi, Apache RocketMQ
sources.notes: Manually vetted CVE dataset. The inventory maps each project slug to a CVE, CWE, repository/tag, buggy commit, fixed commit(s), advisory, and build information. All 120 records are represented as unexecuted candidates here.

sources.name: VJBench
sources.license: NOASSERTION (repository metadata)
sources.notes: The artifact describes 42 reproducible Java vulnerabilities and publishes the CSV inventory with project URL, ID, CVE, CWE, human patch, and CVE URL. All records are represented as unexecuted candidates here.

sources.name: Vul4J
sources.license: CC-BY-4.0 for dataset; GPL-3.0 for code
sources.notes: Real-world Java vulnerability dataset. Current README distinguishes 79 PoV-based entries and 50 SpotBugs-only entries; its CSV carries repository, patch and build/test command metadata. Kept as a source backlog rather than duplicate candidate entries in this first catalog.

sources.name: OWASP Benchmark for Java
sources.license: GPL-2.0
sources.notes: Runnable deliberately vulnerable Java web benchmark. The expected-results manifest labels each test as a true or false vulnerability and CWE. Synthetic controlled source; not represented as real-CVE candidate entries.

sources.name: NIST SARD Juliet Java 1.0
sources.license: Public domain
sources.notes: NIST lists 14,184 Java tests across 106 CWEs. Synthetic control corpus; it should not be presented as a set of real-world CVE cases.

sources.name: VCC-Eval
sources.license: NOASSERTION (repository metadata)
sources.notes: Manually curated vulnerability-introducing-commit data with CVE, CWE, repository, introducing and fixing commits, and affected lines. A rich provenance source, but no build harness is asserted here.
